On a phone: a window and the sheet

annotations.text: The box. A page is a box or a collection; a box is one ground with one compartment per thing on it. The trail above says where you are. Compartments are cut into the tray: walls meet square, the tray's curve only at its corners, less the wall, and the reading inside is cut the same way. Bigger for what matters more. A compartment that is a thing carries a pencil, not a chevron.

The window. Opening does not go anywhere: the same element grows. An opened compartment is a window whatever it holds, and every tool floats in it as a Leaflet-style control: the trail top-left, the camera under it, the compartment's tools on the right edge, the page's tools one stack bottom-right. The reading scrolls under the controls; a picture is bigger than its window. One family of corners, nothing a pill.

The three surfaces. Navigation is what is here: the trail and the chevron. A drawer is editing: a figure, a pin, a face, a row, a thing, opens its properties, shows it is chosen, and what it carries waits in the drawer as one control. A modal is new or delete: the plus asks one question. The filter dims and counts and never hides. The rails step aside for the drawer and the reading scrolls the figure into the clear; the window never changes size.

On a phone the tray is a column, the tray's curve at the top of the first compartment and the foot of the last. The window is at the screen's edge, the drawer a sheet from the foot, and the page behind holds still while either is open.
